data.text/markdown:
Sampling, convergence and performance

Compare PXR/CBS yields for three sampled-history budgets and one adaptive stopping policy. All runs use a 30 keV beam, 100 nm HOPG, 135° observation, and no bremsstrahlung. The 600–2,000 eV band integral is less noisy than individual grid samples. Small CPU budgets illustrate the method, not validated precision; sampled histories are not physical bunch charge.

data.text/markdown:
Adaptive stopping

AdaptiveSampling estimates a batch-means relative standard error (RSE), subject to minimum-sample and contribution guards. It can reach its history limit without meeting the target. The deliberately loose RSE target here is for teaching.

data.text/markdown:
Interpretation

The largest fixed-budget yield is only a reference, not ground truth. These runs share a resolved default seed, so their differences are not an independent-sample error estimate. For uncertainty, use independent seeds and inspect the convergence diagnostics. An adaptive run may stop at its maximum without achieving its RSE target; check its diagnostics. Changing reflection families or energy grids tests systematic discretization, not sampling convergence. Wall times depend on compilation, caching and hardware. The untimed warmup helps, but these are not portable benchmarks. Try increasing the budgets and compare the sampling reference and performance guidance.
